visual_goal: Show fitness functions computed from feeds the estate already produces, landing in one FinDB model, read in one quarterly review that updates the debt register and reads the gates that release or hold tranche funding.
prompt: A left-to-right data-flow illustration. At the far left a column of five small boxes, each with a tiny icon and a short label, top to bottom: 'Pipelines' with a gear icon, 'Delivery ledgers' with a small open book, 'Reconciliation' with two matching checkmarks, 'Control matrix' with a grid icon, 'Ledgers' with a stack of books. Each of the five sends one thin arrow right into a single database cylinder with the word 'FinDB' written once, on the cylinder's front face. Next, one arrow from 'FinDB' into a dashboard with three dial gauges labeled 'Scorecard'. Next, one arrow from 'Scorecard' into a round meeting table labeled 'Quarterly review'. To the right of the review, two items stacked vertically in the same column: on top an open register book labeled 'Debt register', directly below it a turnstile gate labeled 'Tranche gates'. From 'Quarterly review' one arrow up-right into 'Debt register' and one arrow down-right into 'Tranche gates'. One short vertical arrow straight down from 'Debt register' into 'Tranche gates'. At the far right, level with 'Tranche gates', a boardroom table with a stack of coins labeled 'Steering committee', receiving one single arrow, from 'Tranche gates'. Exactly eleven arrows.
alt: Five existing feeds (pipelines, delivery ledgers, reconciliation, control matrix, ledgers) flow into FinDB, which feeds a fitness scorecard read in the quarterly review; the review updates the debt register and reads the tranche gates, which decide funding at the steering committee.

visual_goal: Show the adapted sequencing rule: items with a close external date are weighed against the harm of undated items, the rest are ranked by removal per tranche effort, and the close critical path or a key control breaks ties.
prompt: A left-to-right flow illustration. At the far left a stack of index cards labeled 'Register'. One arrow from it into a gate with a calendar icon labeled 'Date close?'. From 'Date close?' two arrows: one going up-right labeled 'yes' into a balance scale labeled 'Weigh harm now'; one going down-right labeled 'no' into a small flag on a pole labeled 'Latest start'. From 'Weigh harm now' two arrows: one right along the top into a box with a rocket icon labeled 'Brought forward', and one down into a box labeled 'Undated first'. In the middle row, a bar-ranking chart labeled 'Rank by removal' receives one arrow from 'Undated first' and one arrow from 'Latest start'. One arrow from 'Rank by removal' into a magnifying glass over a small clock labeled 'Close path first'. At the far right a neat ordered list on a clipboard labeled 'Ordered list' receives one arrow from 'Brought forward' and one from 'Close path first'. Exactly nine arrows.
alt: Register items pass a date check: if the external date is close, the date is weighed against harm now and the item is brought forward or the undated item goes first; otherwise its latest start is recorded; items are ranked by removal per effort, with the close critical path as tie-break, into an ordered list.

visual_goal: Show a debt register item's life: raised, measured, sequenced, then funded tranche by tranche with a gate read after each, or carried on purpose and re-measured each quarter, until retired.
prompt: A state map drawn as rounded stepping stones along a path from left to right: 'Raised', 'Measured' with a small ruler icon, 'Sequenced', 'Tranche funded' with a small stack of coins, 'Gate read' with a dial gauge icon, and at the far right a green stone 'Retired' with a checkmark. One arrow between each consecutive pair of stones. Below 'Sequenced' a grey stone 'Carried on purpose' with a small note pinned to it, reached by one arrow down from 'Sequenced'; one curved arrow labeled 'quarterly' runs from 'Carried on purpose' back up-left into 'Measured'. Above the path between 'Tranche funded' and 'Gate read' an orange stone 'Redesign': one arrow up from 'Gate read' into 'Redesign' and one arrow down from 'Redesign' into 'Tranche funded'. Below the path, one curved green arrow labeled 'pass' loops from 'Gate read' back into 'Tranche funded'. Exactly ten arrows.
alt: Stepping stones from Raised to Measured, Sequenced, Tranche funded, Gate read and Retired; a gate pass loops back to fund the next tranche, a miss goes through Redesign, and items carried on purpose are re-measured quarterly.
